characteristics.roast: Screen-pressing and baking without wok pan-firing
characteristics.harvestSeason: Mid-spring, slightly later than early bud teas
characteristics.leafWeight: 2–3 g (a few large leaves) per 200 ml

description.short: The largest leaf among China's premier green teas — giant flat blades up to 10 cm long with a delicate orchid aroma
description.overview: Renowned for its extraordinary leaf size (one bud embracing two leaves, meticulously selected for uniformity) and distinct shaping technique — leaves are pressed flat between fine wire meshes rather than rolled.
description.leaf: Remarkably large, straight, two-leaf-and-bud sets 7–10 cm long, deep emerald green with subtle reddish veins and faint mesh markings
description.liquor: Delicate yellow-green, crystal clear and glowing
description.aroma: Pure orchid floral aroma, fresh and sweetly lingering
description.taste: Mild, smooth, and naturally sweet with subtle orchid fragrance and practically zero astringency
description.processing: Strict selection of uniform large shoots (one bud with two leaves) → pan fixation → manual flattening and pressing between cloth or wire mesh screens → multi-stage gentle baking

history.origin: The name translates to 'Monkey Leader of Taiping' — associated in lore with monkeys inhabiting the misty cliffs or honoring the tea master Wang Kuicheng who created the style
history.development: Developed in the early 20th century through careful selection of uniform, robust shoots from the indigenous Shi Da Cha cultivar
history.modern: Awarded a gold medal at the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition, establishing its enduring fame as one of China's Ten Famous Teas
interestingFacts: One of the rare prestigious Chinese green teas prized for colossal leaf size rather than minute tender buds — the exact opposite of common convention
Each individual sprig is traditionally arranged by hand on wire mesh screens to ensure it dries into a pristine, razor-flat shape
